question:
A 43-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department following a high-speed motor vehicle
collision as an unrestrained driver. On arrival, she is non-responsive and intubated, and she is admitted
to the medical intensive care unit for ongoing care, including blood pressure support and mechanical
ventilation. Her identity is later confirmed by a social worker, who contacts her immediate family
members. After multiple family members arrive, the medical team informs them that the patient is
unlikely to achieve a full recovery due to significant brain function loss observed on neuroimaging. The
patient has remained unconscious throughout her hospitalization. The care team is considering a
tracheostomy and gastrostomy tube placement for enteral feeding; however, the family members
disagree on how to proceed. Among the following individuals, who has the highest priority to serve as
the surrogate decision-maker in this situation? Answer Choices: (A) Cousin who is the closest living
blood relative (B) Brother with power of attorney for financial decisions (C) Adult niece who is a
healthcare provider (D) Adopted son (E) Father (F) Boyfriend (G) Close friend designated as
emergency contact (H) Sister (I) Domestic partner of 5 years (J) Ex-husband who shares custody of
children
 A. Close friend designated as emergency contact
B. Cousin who is the closest living blood relative
C. Father
D. Brother with power of attorney for financial decisions
E. Adult niece who is a healthcare provider
F. Boyfriend
G. Adopted son
H. Domestic partner of 5 years
I. Ex-husband who shares custody of children

J. Sister
